findings: NTT DATA / Penn State 29th Annual Third-Party Logistics Study 2025 (PDF, fully processed via markitdown): discusses outsourcing trends, likelihood to switch providers (13% very likely, 29% likely, 32% somewhat likely to switch based on AI capabilities), barriers to change — but contains NO percentage-of-freight-spend switching cost figure anywhere in the document.
CSCMP State of Logistics Report and 3PL Study are available for purchase; no free executive summary discloses a switching cost percentage.

Academic paper 'The role of switching costs in third-party logistics' (IJAOM, 2025, Inderscience): quantitative study of 202 UK firms, focuses on power dynamics and satisfaction — abstract does not mention a percentage-of-freight-spend metric; full text is paywalled.
AWI Logistics trade blog cites $25K-$100K in absolute switching costs (contract termination, inventory transfer) — not expressed as % of freight spend and not a primary source.
No government, multilateral, or audited primary source provides a 3-8% (or any %) switching cost benchmark relative to annual freight spend.
The 3-8% range in the original claim has zero traceable primary citation and is not corroborated by any source found across 4 searches and 1 full PDF review.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: No audited switching cost estimate publicly disclosed; the NTT DATA / Penn State 29th Annual Third-Party Logistics Study (2025) and CSCMP research confirm that 3PL transitions involve high-touch change management complexity — 74% of shippers report only moderate or lower organizational receptiveness to change — but no primary source publishes a specific percentage-of-freight-spend switching cost figure. ARC Advisory Group and trade press describe transition costs as highly context-dependent.
suggested_revision_options.note: This is the orchestrator-specified fallback language, substantiated by NTT DATA 3PL Study 2025 data on change management barriers.

suggested_revision_options.revised_claim_text: [ASSUMED-N]: 3PL switching cost estimated at 3-8% of annual freight spend — to validate: commission primary research via CSCMP, ARC Advisory Group, or shipper survey; no publicly available primary source corroborates this range.

suggested_revision_options.rationale: The 3-8% figure is entirely unsubstantiated after exhaustive search across industry studies, academic literature, and trade press. Remove from artifact or replace with the qualitative fallback.

sub_claims.reasoning: After processing the full NTT DATA / Penn State 29th Annual 3PL Study 2025 (4,241 lines) and searching CSCMP, academic, and trade sources, the 3-8% of freight spend figure cannot be traced to any primary source. The orchestrator-specified fallback language is more defensible and is now directly supported by quantitative data from the NTT DATA 3PL Study on organizational resistance to 3PL transitions (only 23% of shippers report being extremely receptive to change). The percentage range should be dropped and replaced with the qualitative statement.

sources_evaluated.key_data: 82% of shipper freight transportation outsourced; 74% of shippers only moderately or less receptive to organizational change; 13%+29%+32%=74% of shippers likely to switch 3PL based on AI capabilities — but NO switching cost as % of freight spend figure.

e2open FY2025: subscription revenue $528.0M (down 1.6% YoY), total revenue $607.7M, 500,000 connected enterprises, 18B annual transactions. Control tower not separately reported. No per-customer ACV disclosed.
sources_evaluated.note: Confirms e2open does not publicly disclose control tower ACV or customer count; this makes the 10-K route for per-customer pricing unavailable without attended fetch.

sources_evaluated.publisher: International Journal of Advanced Operations Management
sources_evaluated.key_data: Qualitative/quantitative study of switching costs in UK 3PL relationships (n=202); focuses on power dynamics, not % of freight spend. Paywalled — abstract only reviewed.
CSCMP 2024 Third-Party Logistics Study — purchase required; no public executive summary with switching cost %.

overall_assessment: Both sub-claims remain without primary-source support after exhaustive search. Sub-claim A (control tower pricing $200K-$500K+) is trade-blog-only with no methodology; all analyst firms and vendors use opaque enterprise pricing. Sub-claim B (3-8% switching cost) has zero traceable primary source; the most relevant publicly available industry study (NTT DATA 29th Annual 3PL Study 2025, fully reviewed) contains no such figure. Recommended treatment: mark claim A as ASSUMED-N, replace claim B with orchestrator-specified qualitative fallback supported by NTT DATA 3PL Study quantitative change-management data.
